\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نرمش} \fa{کردن} (narmesh kardan)}{نرمش کردن (narmesh kardan)}]{\fa{نرمش} \fa{کردن} (narmesh kardan) — to stretch, to do light exercises}

\label{lesson:FA-C516-narmesh-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to wrestle, then the Persian for weightlifting.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نرمش} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{نرمش} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{narmesh kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to stretch, to do light exercises\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قبل} \fa{از} \fa{دویدن} \fa{نرمش} \fa{میکنم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qabl az davidan narmesh mikonam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I stretch before running.
\end{quote}

\emph{narmesh} 'suppleness', from \emph{narm} 'soft', + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{narmesh} is built on native Persian \emph{narm}, 'soft', with the noun ending \emph{-esh}: softening the body. EtymDB has no entry for it. \emph{kardan} is inherited.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{narmesh kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{narmesh kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{narmesh kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to wrestle, then the Persian for weightlifting, then say \emph{narmesh kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{یوگا} (yogâ)}{یوگا (yogâ)}]{\fa{یوگا} (yogâ) — yoga}

\label{lesson:FA-C516-yoga}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for weightlifting, then the Persian for to stretch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{یوگا}}
\textbf{\fa{یوگا}} (\emph{yogâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}yoga\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادرم} \fa{هفته} \fa{ای} \fa{سه} \fa{بار} \fa{یوگا} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâdaram hafte-i se bâr yogâ mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother does yoga three times a week.
\end{quote}

\emph{yogâ kardan} — to do yoga.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{yogâ} is a modern loan, usually traced through English to Sanskrit \emph{yoga}, 'yoking, joining'. EtymDB has no entry for the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تناسب} \fa{اندام} (tanâsob-e andâm)}{تناسب اندام (tanâsob-e andâm)}]{\fa{تناسب} \fa{اندام} (tanâsob-e andâm) — fitness, being in shape}

\label{lesson:FA-C516-tanasob-e-andam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to stretch, then the Persian for yoga.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تناسب} \fa{اندام}}
\textbf{\fa{تناسب} \fa{اندام}} (\emph{tanâsob-e andâm}) — \textquotedblleft{}fitness, being in shape\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{برای} \fa{تناسب} \fa{اندام} \fa{شنا} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u barâ-ye tanâsob-e andâm shenâ mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She swims to keep fit.
\end{quote}

\emph{tanâsob} 'proportion' (Arabic) + \emph{andâm} 'body, figure' (Persian).

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tanâsob-e andâm} is built in Persian on \emph{tanâsob}, 'proportion', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{tanāsub}, and native \emph{andâm}, 'body, figure'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پرانرژی} (porenerzhi)}{پرانرژی (porenerzhi)}]{\fa{پرانرژی} (porenerzhi) — energetic, full of energy}

\label{lesson:FA-C516-porenerzhi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for yoga, then the Persian for fitness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پرانرژی}}
\textbf{\fa{پرانرژی}} (\emph{porenerzhi}) — \textquotedblleft{}energetic, full of energy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{صبحها} \fa{پرانرژی} \fa{هستند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachchehâ sobhhâ porenerzhi hastand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children are full of energy in the mornings.
\end{quote}

\emph{por} 'full' + \emph{enerzhi} 'energy'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{porenerzhi} is built in Persian on native \emph{por}, 'full', and \emph{enerzhi}, 'energy', which was borrowed from French \emph{énergie} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تنبلی} \fa{کردن} (tanbali kardan)}{تنبلی کردن (tanbali kardan)}]{\fa{تنبلی} \fa{کردن} (tanbali kardan) — to be lazy, to slack}

\label{lesson:FA-C516-tanbali-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for fitness, then the Persian for energetic.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تنبلی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تنبلی} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tanbali kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be lazy, to slack\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{امروز} \fa{تنبلی} \fa{کردم} \fa{و} \fa{ورزش} \fa{نکردم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{emruz tanbali kardam va varzesh nakardam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Today I was lazy and didn't exercise.
\end{quote}

\emph{tanbal} 'lazy' + \emph{-i} + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tanbali} is built on \emph{tanbal}, 'lazy', with the noun ending \emph{-i}. EtymDB lists \emph{tanbal} without a source, and its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
